verdict: Directional consistency confirmed: physics and data agree on positive reinforcement; the large modulus-to-strength magnitude ratio is the expected modulus != strength gap, so the surrogate validates the reinforcement trend, not pointwise strength.
caveats: Halpin-Tsai predicts elastic modulus, not failure strength; only the reinforcement trend (sign + order of magnitude) is cross-checked.
A deterministic surrogate cannot validate a probabilistic prediction on its own; the Bayesian framework supplies the omitted uncertainty.
Absolute-strength micromechanics requires interfacial parameters (interfacial shear strength, critical fibre length) not recoverable from the literature dataset.
